newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Aranypok sees profit, dividend up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Aranypok sees profit, dividend up in 1997.

text.p: Shareholders of Hungarian clothes retailer Aranypok Rt on Wednesday approved the payout of a seven percent dividend on 1996 earnings and for 1997 the company plans higher dividend on higher profits.
"For 1997 we plan a pre-tax profit of 90 million forints with sales revenues rising by 15 percent to 2.45 billion forints," Aranypok's Deputy General Director Marta Novak told Reuters.
In 1996 Aranypok had a pre-tax profit of 80.3 million forints and an after-tax profit of 60.9 million.
In 1997 the company will continue its policy of gradual increase in dividend ratios.
"At the time of our bourse listing we undertook to provide our shareholders with a gradually rising dividend level," Novak said. "For 1997 we plan to pay a nine percent dividend."
Novak said the company's sales rose by 10 percent in the first quarter of 1997 over the same period of 1996 and added that Aranypok was changing its price policy to attract customers.
"Although our regular clients are upper middle class...we change minimally our pricing policy and offer cheaper products in some shops -- but not the downtown ones," she said.

The company now operates 30 traditional and one discount shop in Budapest and is to open its first one outside the capital, in Esztergom under franchise soon, Novak said, adding Aranypok considered to establish itself in Budapest's mushrooming shopping malls, as well.
On the Budapest Stocks Exchange Aranypok shares close at 7,550 forints on Tuesday.
